body: THE TRUE-BUT-WRONG PICK DRILL 1 OF 6 SUBJECT Criminal Law & Procedure SUBTOPIC Constitutional Protection of Accused Persons DIFFICULTY ▮▮▮▮▮ Private Bookstore Plea BARMATRIX Q# 14555 — Christian variation: 14555_private_bookstore_plea Daniel was indicted in state court in January 2025 for the robbery and murder of Stephen, which occurred in December 2022 during the closing shift at Lydia’s private Christian bookstore. Daniel retained Mary as counsel. Mary filed a motion to dismiss on the ground that Daniel had been prejudiced by the 25-month delay in obtaining the indictment. Thereafter, Daniel, with Mary present, appeared in court for arraignment and stated that he wished to plead guilty. The presiding judge, Esther, asked Daniel whether he understood the nature of the charges, possible defenses, and maximum allowable sentences. Daniel replied that he did, and Judge Esther reviewed all of those matters with him. Judge Esther then asked Daniel whether he understood that he did not have to plead guilty. Daniel responded that he knew that. The judge accepted the plea and sentenced Daniel to 25 years. Six months later, Daniel filed a motion to set aside his guilty plea on each of the following grounds. Which ground provides a constitutional basis for relief? A The judge did not rule

buttons.text: AThe judge did not rule on Daniel’s motion to dismiss before accepting the guilty plea.
BThe judge did not determine that Daniel had robbed and killed Stephen.
CThe judge did not determine whether Daniel understood that he had a right to a jury trial.
DThe judge did not determine whether the prosecutor’s file contained any undisclosed exculpatory mat
